entities.name: Blaise of Sebaste
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Blaise of Sebaste was a renowned physician and bishop of Sebastea in historical Lesser Armenia, venerated as a Christian saint and martyr since the 4th century. As one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, he played a pivotal role in the spread of Christianity in the region.


Born in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE, Blaise's life was marked by his unwavering dedication to his faith and his work as a healer. He is particularly noted for his miraculous cure of a leper, which led to his subsequent ordination as a bishop. Following his death in 316 CE, Blaise's legacy continued to inspire and protect the people of Sebastea, solidifying his place as a revered figure in Armenian Orthodox tradition.


Blaise's story has been passed down through the centuries, with his feast day celebrated on February 2nd. His life and martyrdom serve as a testament to the enduring power of faith and the importance of compassion in the face of suffering.
